VOYAGER VERSUS

A chat-controlled spaceship battle game for your stream. Two viewers pilot animated ships using Twitch chat, with laser fire, missiles, shield boosts, evasive rolls and a winner reveal.

Use the downloaded local package for your stream. The hosted version is a playable preview. Your local launcher runs the actual shared game, connects to Streamer.bot and serves the OBS overlay. Keep it open while streaming.

Get started on your OBS PC

  1. Install Node.js 22.4 or newer. No npm packages or separate Python installation are needed.
  2. Extract Voyager-Versus.zip into a writable folder, for example C:\Voyager-Versus. Do not run from inside the ZIP.
  3. Open Streamer.bot. Ensure your Twitch broadcaster account is connected.
  4. In Streamer.bot, open Servers/Clients → WebSocket Server. Start the server. Defaults are address 127.0.0.1, port 8080 and endpoint /. Keep your existing password settings; the game supports authentication.
  5. Double-click START-VOYAGER.bat. A terminal stays open and your control panel opens at http://127.0.0.1:8740/.
  6. In the game's Stream setup tab, enter your Streamer.bot WebSocket address and password if enabled, then click Connect chat. Wait for “Streamer.bot connected · Twitch chat ready”.
  7. Use Open training preview for an isolated animation test. The live arena waits for a viewer to type !versus in Twitch chat; a different viewer must type !versus to claim the second seat.

Chat controls need no command imports, Twitch token or OBS WebSocket connection. Voyager balance payouts and availability announcements require the C# action setup below. The game listens to chat events already received by Streamer.bot. It posts readiness, initiator/challenger confirmations, match summaries and verified reward confirmations through the updated v2.5 action.

Add it to OBS

  1. Add a Browser Source called Voyager Versus.
  2. Leave Local file unchecked. Paste http://127.0.0.1:8740/?overlay=1&hideIdle=1 as the URL.
  3. For native 4K, select Ultra graphics in Stream setup and set source width to 3840, height to 2160. Start at 30 FPS; try 60 FPS if your GPU has headroom. Balanced quality uses 2048px maps and a 1920px render cap. Copy the quality URL into OBS after choosing it.
  4. Resize and position the source within your scene. For your 32:9 stream layout, the 16:9 arena can occupy half the screen or be enlarged within a dedicated game scene. At 5120 × 1440 it centres a 16:9 arena with transparent side space.
  5. Keep the launcher running. The control panel can be closed, and refreshing the OBS source will reconnect to the same ongoing battle.
Optional overlay behaviourURL addition
Keep the idle arena visible (idle hiding is on by default)&hideIdle=0
Enable sound control&sound=1

The overlay is always fully transparent, including with existing OBS URLs. There is no background setting to enable. The space backdrop, challenger-screen fill, header/footer panels, scene borders, scanlines, empty meter tracks, winner backplate and pause-screen tint are removed. Ships, effects, logos, names and game information float over your stream. Use Stream setup to change idle hiding or sound. Replace the game files while retaining local/data, restart the launcher, then refresh the OBS Browser Source cache. If you previously added Custom CSS that paints a background in OBS, remove it; no chroma key filter is needed. For audio, use OBS Interact once and click Enable sound. Enable “Control audio via OBS” in the Browser Source if you want a separate mixer channel. Keep dashboard sound off to avoid doubled audio. A browser-source reload can require audio to be enabled again.

OBS cooldown timer

Add a second Browser Source named Voyager Versus Cooldown. Leave Local file unchecked and use http://127.0.0.1:8740/cooldown.html, width 640, height 240. Position it anywhere on your stream. Its background is completely transparent; no chroma key is needed. Copy this URL from Stream setup or the Voyager Versus page in Control. If you changed VOYAGER_PORT, use the matching port.

The timer reads the same saved 45-minute deadline as the game and counts down in minutes and seconds. At zero it shows READY · Type !versus to call for a challenger once the arena is idle, entries are open and Streamer.bot is connected. Paused/closed entries, training, current battles and disconnected chat show their actual state. While a challenger call is open, its second pilot can still join immediately; the timer is for the next new call.

Keep the Voyager host running. OBS refreshes, scene changes and host restarts read the existing deadline; they never start a new countdown. A lost host connection shows a reconnecting status instead of an unconfirmed READY prompt. This source only reads state: it never starts games, awards points or sends chat messages. For a harmless visual test, open Preview timer; this labelled 12-second preview is separate from the live timer. Do not include ?preview=1 in the OBS live URL.

Viewer commands

Commands on the battle overlay: during the 10-second launch countdown and active battle, a transparent guide beneath the ships shows !fire, !missile, !shield and !dodge, with their recharge times. The footer shows !leave to forfeit; each pilot’s HUD shows their current weapon recharge. The guide says when weapons unlock at launch or commands are paused, and hides during the waiting splash, idle arena and results. The existing OBS battle URL is unchanged. After updating, restart Voyager and refresh the OBS Browser Source cache.

CommandWhat happens
!versusWhen idle, open the challenger splash as Pilot 1. The next different viewer to use !versus becomes Pilot 2, starting a 10-second countdown and then a 30-second battle.
!ship interceptorSelect 100 hull / 50 shield before joining.
!ship sentinelSelect 120 hull / 30 shield before joining.
!ship phantomSelect 85 hull / 65 shield before joining.
!firePulse lasers: 14 damage, 10 energy, 2-second cooldown.
!missilePlasma missile: 32 damage, 35 energy, 10-second cooldown.
!shieldRestore up to 30 shield, 30 energy, 12-second cooldown.
!dodgeEvade incoming hits for 2.5 seconds, 25 energy, 9-second cooldown.
!leaveCancel your open challenger call. During a battle or countdown, this forfeits the match.

Commands are case-insensitive. Only the two active pilots can attack. Feedback, recharge timers and actions appear on the overlay and in the combat feed.

The challenger splash

The first !versus shows the pilot’s name and chosen ship, an animated radar and a large !versus prompt. The splash stays visible until a different viewer claims the second seat, the caller types !leave, or you press Cancel call / Clear call. There is no waiting timeout.

The next eligible !versus user is assigned immediately. No additional acceptance command is needed. Repeated commands from the first pilot cannot fill both seats, and further !versus commands cannot replace locked pilots during the countdown, battle or winner screen. New live calls share a 45-minute cooldown, starting when Pilot 1 calls. The challenger can join immediately. The next call needs both an idle arena and an expired cooldown. Cancelling a call does not reset the cooldown; neither does pausing, refreshing OBS or restarting the same local host. Only an exact, standalone !versus starts or joins a live call. !join, !duel and !accept are disabled. Cooldown expiry, readiness announcements and page refreshes never launch a match.

By default, the “Hide overlay until someone calls !versus” option hides the idle arena and automatically reveals the calling screen, countdown, battle and results. The same existing OBS source is used throughout. A refreshed overlay reconnects to the current calling screen or countdown.

Battle rules

  • A 10-second countdown begins when two pilots are matched. Default round length is 30 seconds, with an 8-second winner screen.
  • Each ship starts with 150 combined hull and shield, and 100 energy. Energy regenerates at 8 per second. Shield boost cannot exceed that ship's shield maximum.
  • With automatic fire enabled, each ship fires a free 8-damage shot every 4 seconds. Viewer commands add stronger attacks; this keeps combat moving despite stream delay.
  • Damage drains shields first, then hull. Hull cannot be repaired during a round. The first ship to lose all hull loses. At timeout, the higher remaining hull + shield total wins. Equal totals draw.
  • Manual weapon cooldowns are per weapon. A general 0.65-second input limit prevents repeated command floods. Invalid commands are ignored; cooldown feedback is rate-limited in the feed.
  • There is no automatic matchmaking queue. Every live match needs a fresh !versus from its initiator and then a different challenger.
  • Pausing freezes gameplay timers and commands. The 45-minute global cooldown continues in real time. “Close entries” stops new !versus entries but lets an active match continue. “Cancel call” dismisses a waiting challenger splash. “End battle” cancels the active match without changing rankings. “Clear call” cancels the waiting challenger call.

Install the v2.5 rewards action

  1. Stop the Voyager launcher and back up your working folder, including local/data.
  2. In Streamer.bot, disable older Voyager Versus Rewards actions. Keep their saved variables and receipts.
  3. Import Voyager-Versus-Rewards-Install.sb. Select its action and dedicated queue, both named Voyager Versus Rewards v2.5.
  4. Open the new action’s enabled Execute C# Code sub-action, then Compile → Save. Keep the action enabled, Concurrent off, no triggers, and its Blocking queue unpaused.
  5. Restart the launcher, refresh the page, reconnect Streamer.bot and click Stream setup → Check rewards action. Look for Rewards v2.5 verified. This check makes no test payment.
  6. Pending wins retry automatically at 50 Voyager points. Use Rewards & repair → Check saved history → Apply eligible credits for older history. Runner-up entitlement is 0. Read the complete update guide for troubleshooting.

Each reward retains its existing durable receipt and requires a verified persisted balance increase. Direct broadcasts and temporary global responses both confirm execution. If neither arrives, the credit remains pending for a later receipt check. No receipt is cleared to force a repeat payment.

The global call interval is fixed at 45 minutes. When the cooldown expires, the game waits for a new !versus call. An open call’s challenger is exempt, and demo battles neither consume nor wait for the live cooldown.

When !versus becomes available

The local host posts: “Voyager Versus is ready! Type !versus to call for a challenger. Winner: 50 Voyager points | Runner-up: 0 points. New calls every 45 minutes.”

The message posts once per available window, including the first ready connection. It waits until the 45-minute cooldown has expired, the arena is idle, entries are open, the game is unpaused and Twitch is connected. It does not repeat while the arena remains idle, on dashboard refresh, or after a normal host restart. A new live call starts the next 45-minute window. Demo battles do not consume that window or create extra announcements.

If disconnected at expiry, the message waits for reconnection and checks the arena is still available. Both the host and Streamer.bot keep announcement receipts to avoid duplicate sends. If the connection fails during a send and confirmation is uncertain, the panel flags the announcement for review rather than posting repeated messages. The action expires queued announcements after 10 seconds and the host retries only while still ready. Keep the launcher and Streamer.bot running.

Upgrading from a 20-minute version preserves the original call time and extends its interval to 45 minutes. Historical unpaid wins are revised to 50 points and runner-up entries to 0; use Rewards & repair to verify receipts and apply the backfill. Zero-point runner-up results are not queued as payments. Existing cooldowns extend to 45 minutes from the original call time once, including after a restart.

Pending rewards and recovery

Rewards are saved on the host before dispatch. If Streamer.bot is disconnected or the action is missing, they stay queued and resume when the connection and action are available. Each payout carries a unique receipt, so retrying after a lost connection does not repeat a completed payment. Keep the launcher open for pending confirmations.

A needs review status means a missing Twitch ID, storage problem or ambiguous receipt. Use the Rewards & repair page and inspect the original points movement before using Review unpaid claim. See UPDATE_2_0.txt. Preserve receipts and local/data so the verification and duplicate-payment checks remain intact.

The included action uses the existing points balance and posts ready and match messages through your bot account, with broadcaster fallback. Your existing Voyager ledger’s variable listeners can observe these balance changes.

Rankings and your Voyager programme

Live wins, losses and draws are saved in local/data/rankings.json. The panel shows and exports the top 50 pilots. Back up the entire local/data folder if moving PCs. It also contains economy.json, which preserves the cooldown and reward outbox. When updating the game, stop the launcher, replace the program files and retain your existing local/data folder. Use one host instance per channel. Ship selections, open calls and current battles reset when the host closes. Connection passwords are kept only in memory and must be re-entered after restarting.

Demo battles and simulated test pilots do not affect rankings. Completed live battles with a winner add 50 Voyager points to the winner; the runner-up receives 0 through the rewards action. The action increments the winner’s existing persisted Twitch user variable points, identified by Twitch user ID. It never resets their balance. Draws, host cancellations, training, simulated pilots and forfeits during the launch countdown receive no payout. A forfeit after launch awards the normal winner and runner-up amounts. Membership groups, Twitch VIPs and giveaway settings are unchanged. Twitch is the supported chat platform for this first version.

Test without going live

From the live panel choose “Open training preview”. In that separate page, use “Launch training demo” to preview the calling splash for four seconds, automatically add a training challenger, then run the 10-second countdown and battle. These tests do not run on the live OBS source. For manual testing in that preview, type !versus as pilot_one in Sandbox Comms to display the splash, change the name to pilot_two, and send !versus again. Once the countdown ends, send the battle commands as either pilot. Simulated pilots also perform automatic tactical actions to keep the test moving.

The hosted preview runs separately in each browser tab. It is for trying the game, and cannot directly connect to your local Streamer.bot. Use the local control panel for stream setup.

Troubleshooting

ProblemCheck
“node is not recognised”Install Node.js 22.4+ and run the launcher again. You may need to reopen your terminal after installation.
“Cannot reach Streamer.bot”Start its WebSocket Server and match the host, port and endpoint. Streamer.bot's WebSocket port is normally 8080; OBS's 4455 port is a different service.
Password required / authentication failedEnter the password configured for the Streamer.bot WebSocket Server. It is not your Twitch password.
Connected, but commands do nothingConfirm Streamer.bot is receiving chat from the correct Twitch broadcaster account, entries are open, and the game is not paused. Test !versus from two different real Twitch accounts. A simulated training call cannot be joined by a live viewer. Shared-chat guest messages and Streamer.bot test events are ignored.
Chat disconnects during a live matchThe host pauses the arena. Reconnect Streamer.bot, then press Resume. Reconnection never silently restarts the match.
OBS source is blankConfirm the terminal is still running and the URL matches. If idle hiding is enabled, type !versus or launch a demo to reveal the overlay. Use a URL Browser Source, not a local HTML file.
Port 8740 already in useCheck whether Voyager is already running. Otherwise set VOYAGER_PORT to another free port before launching and use that port in both URLs.
Streamer.bot is on another PCRun the Voyager launcher on the OBS PC. Enter the other PC's LAN WebSocket address, and configure Streamer.bot to listen on its LAN interface with authentication. The game control panel itself remains accessible only on the OBS PC.
Sound missingAdd &sound=1, use OBS Interact, click Enable sound, and check the OBS mixer. Sound is off by default.

Visual identity

Voyager Versus uses your Voyager, MDA009 and Unprofessionals emblems, with Rajdhani lettering, royal blue, midnight navy, cyan lighting and silver details from your stream branding references. The font files and logos are included locally, so the game and OBS overlay do not rely on Google Fonts loading over the network. Blue and silver identify the two pilots; each ship retains its own artwork and engine colour.

Voyager Control

The updated Voyager Control package includes a Voyager Versus page in its sidebar and a START-VOYAGER-CONTROL.bat launcher. Use its VERSUS_SETUP.html guide to move your existing local/data folder into the bundled game before starting. The standalone launcher in this package continues to work independently.

Package contents

START-VOYAGER.bat — Windows launcher
start-voyager.sh — macOS/Linux launcher (run sh start-voyager.sh)
dist/ — control panel, game, guide and OBS visuals
local/ — authoritative game host and Streamer.bot adapter
tests/ — automated checks (run node --test tests/*.test.mjs)

Verification: automated battle-rule, WebSocket protocol and local HTTP/SSE checks completed during creation. Live Twitch, C# compilation in your installed Streamer.bot, real balance credits, OBS rendering and audio need a test on your streaming PC. No connection to your PC has been made.
